title: Sum of Good Subsequences
summary: Given an integer array, calculate the sum of all subsequences where the absolute difference between consecutive elements is exactly 1, modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Given an integer array, calculate the sum of all subsequences where the absolute difference between consecutive elements is exactly 1, modulo 10^9 + 7. A subsequence of size 1 is considered good.
constraints: A nonempty subsequence is good when every consecutive selected-value difference has absolute value exactly one.
Return the sum of elements over all index-distinct good subsequences modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: For each ending value, retain both the number of good subsequences and their total element sum.
A new value x starts alone or extends sequences ending at x-1 and x+1.
For each neighbor, add its old sums plus x times its sequence count; accumulate under endpoint x.
These are exactly the legal predecessors, and processing left to right preserves subsequence index order.
editorial: These are exactly the legal predecessors, and processing left to right preserves subsequence index order.

tests.explanation: The three singletons and subsequences 1,2; 2,1; and 1,2,1 contribute fourteen.
Three singletons, two adjacent pairs, and the full sequence contribute forty.
